articles.title: Australia’s first fashion library’s rule for borrowers? No stylists allowed
articles.summary: Being able to touch and examine garments in person can be a vital source of inspiration for designers. Now a collection which does just that has relocated from Europe to Melbourne. In what was once a nun’s bedroom, a long-sleeved, slate-blue Hermès dress from the 1970s hangs beside a window.
body: The private collection of fashion items, amassed over a decade of travel, is available for rent by designers and fashion students seeking inspiration. Its curator and owner, fashion designer Hannah Canham, has lived and worked across North America (in New York and Los Angeles) and Europe (in Madrid, Berlin, London and Paris) where designer archives are commonplace.

She has been running the archive since 2018, but in 2024 she returned home to Melbourne with her treasure trove of approximately 1,000 pieces in tow. She reopened the archive for commercial use in March. While museum and educational institutions already house garment collections, This Era Archive is the first of its kind in Australia.

“In Australia it’s new information for some designers,” Canham says. “Whereas working in Europe, this is part of their design process. They start each season by looking for inspiration, going to museums, reading old books and going to archives.”
There are two ideas at the heart of the project: that fashion is self-referential and cyclical; and that the best design needs to be touched to be properly understood.
points: Being able to touch and examine garments in person can be a vital source of inspiration for designers.
Now a collection which does just that has relocated from Europe to Melbourne.

articles.title: The moment I knew: I’d lost his number and was about to switch off my old phone for good – then a text pinged
articles.summary: When Karen Bleakley locked eyes with Matt on the dancefloor, it was a sign of a new beginning. But when she lost his number, she thought she’d never see him again. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: In 2002 I was in the midst of a messy breakup, so my friend Clare did what friends do – she took me out, fed me shots and showed me a good time.

We were at Route 66, a cheesy nightclub in Portsmouth on the southern coast of the UK, that was blasting 80s tunes. Then on the dancefloor I saw him: a young, hunky Ryan Phillippe lookalike, if Ryan Phillippe had spent the summer windsurfing. Matt, a Portsmouth local, was all blond curls, tanned skin and bright blue eyes that caught mine as I stared at him.
Within minutes we were dancing, and we barely left each other’s sides for the rest of the night.

A group of us ended up at my friend’s flat, where Matt passed an important test: sharing a piece of toast and Marmite with me as we all partied through the night. I’d never dated anyone who could stand Marmite before, so this seemed promising.
points: When Karen Bleakley locked eyes with Matt on the dancefloor, it was a sign of a new beginning.
But when she lost his number, she thought she’d never see him again.

articles.title: This off-brand camp stove is better than a Jetboil for hot coffee in the great outdoors
articles.summary: When temps drop, there’s nothing better than a steaming hot beverage especially when camping and the Camp Chef Stryker outperforms JetBoil every time. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I have trudged through camping without a lot of things: clean socks, dry shoes, a headlamp. But in temperatures when you can see your breath in the morning, skipping hot coffee is a hair too far. So when my Jetboil Flash stove sputtered out of gas on a car-camping trip years ago, it was worth the hour-long drive into the nearest town for more.

Or would have been, if I had found any. While every gas station and general store I stopped in carried the cheap, ubiquitous green bottles of propane, the Jetboil’s fussy isobutane canisters were nowhere to be found.

After gritting out the rest of the trip on cold instant coffee, I knew there had to be a better way, and found it: the Camp Chef Stryker. Just as fast as the vaunted Jetboil, but cheaper and easier to fuel, it’s hands down the best way to heat up water anywhere, for anything from coffee to ramen.
I have used antiquated white fuel stoves, cheap Amazon stoves and even built my own methanol stove out of a Rolling Rock can. None of them compare to a stove and pot built to work together.
points: When temps drop, there’s nothing better than a steaming hot beverage especially when camping and the Camp Chef Stryker outperforms JetBoil every time.

articles.title: When Dad asked me to edit his novel, I wanted to say no – but ran directly towards the lion’s den | Anna Spargo-Ryan
articles.summary: My father doesn’t ask for help from just anyone. And yet he asked for mine. He believed in me. My dad and I believe in many of the same things: cheesecake; the Geelong football club; my mum. And that we should immediately be experts at anything. First try. No practice. No revision.
body: So when he asked, at age 77, if I would edit the novel he’d been working on, I responded with what I’ll generously call abject terror. I knew, from teaching hundreds of later-life would-be writers, that there would be feedback. Good Lord, would there. And I also knew, from a lifetime of being explicitly told, that we always got things right the first time. No exceptions.

I wanted to say no. I wanted to tell him, Dad, our relationship is too precious to me. “I’m not sure I have time,” I said, because I am the worst daughter on Earth. But, after my life had flashed before my eyes, I took a beat. The truth is: his outrageous self-belief is well founded. Most people are worse than him at most things. My dad doesn’t ask for help from just anyone. And yet, he had asked for mine.
He didn’t just believe in cake and footy and my mum. He believed in me.
So I did a 180. I ran directly towards the lion’s den. “Sure,” I said, impaling myself on the sword of my dad’s validation, “I would love to edit your novel.”

articles.title: Consciously Coupled: Owen Thiele and Jared Ellner on Working Side by Side and Being Gemini-for-Scorpio
articles.summary: The “Adults” star and his stylist partner—who’s dressed everyone from Sabrina Carpenter to Olivia Rodrigo to Thiele himself—have been dating since college.
body: It’s the age-old question that’s sparked a thousand romance novels and lovelorn midnight Google searches: how do you make a relationship work? Especially when both parties are very busy? In this column, we’ll be talking to some of our favorite star-for-star pairs about how they work together, inspire each other, and navigate love in the public eye.

It’s been a big summer for Owen Thiele, arguably the breakout star of the recently released second season of FX’s Adults. But things are no less busy for Thiele’s partner, Jared Ellner, a stylist known for dressing everyone from Sabrina Carpenter and Olivia Rodrigo to Emma Chamberlain.

Thiele and Ellner, who have been dating since college, some 11 years ago (“I dropped out two weeks after I got there, but in those two weeks, I met Jared Ellner, so it was worth the tuition,” jokes Thiele), and who live together in Los Angeles, are linked by more than romance: Ellner is also Thiele’s stylist. So it’s safe to say the two have learned quite a bit over the years about how to balance work and love.
points: The “Adults” star and his stylist partner—who’s dressed everyone from Sabrina Carpenter to Olivia Rodrigo to Thiele himself—have been dating since college.

articles.title: At Venice Film Festival, Amal Clooney and Emma Corrin Joined a Star-Studded Toast to the Cartier Cinema Club
articles.summary: The stars—including Chloé Zhao, Kate Mara, and Orlando Bloom—stepped out to celebrate Cartier’s fifth year as the main sponsor of the Venice Film Festival at the Gritti Palace last night.
body: Che bello! On Friday night, a glittering cast of film and fashion talents elegantly made their way onto the dock of the Gritti Palace from an army of grumbling water taxis, ready to celebrate Cartier ’s fifth year as main sponsor of the Venice Film Festival —and the launch of the fine jewelry house’s brand-new Cartier Cinema Club.

But most of all, it was an opportunity for many of the biggest stars whose films are premiering this week, as well as some of the jury members—including composer Daniel Blumberg and his girlfriend, Taylor Russell—to sit back, sip a negroni, catch up with friends, and watch the reflection of the grand Santa Maria della Salute church on the opposite bank shimmering in the black waters of the Grand Canal. That’s why Venice is often referred to as the most glamorous film festival in the world.

articles.title: The Best On-Court Style Moments Served at the 2026 U.S. Open
articles.summary: The 2026 U.S. Open is in full swing! With Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, and Venus Williams in play, don’t expect traditional tennis whites on the hard court.
body: Ready, set…style. The 2026 U.S. Open is in full swing in Queens, New York City, with the season already serveing up some thrilling,—and stylish—moments.

Serena Williams made her return with doubles partner Carlos Alcaraz, who was back in it after an injury that struck him out of this year’s Wimbledon. The duo sported some striking matching royal purple and black Nike kits. Roger Federer played a once-in-a-lifetime exhibition match at the Arthur Ashe Stadium with Lorenzo Musetti—and also launched a limited-edition version of On’s The Roger shoe —before absconding to Rhode Island to be inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

Across the next few days, we’ll see the likes of women’s world number one Aryna Sabalenka, Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, Venus Williams, Taylor Fritz, and more hit the Flushing Meadows hard court. The Williams sisters were at the forefront of subverting traditional tennis whites. Gauff debuted her latest New Balance x Miu Miu on the London grass, while Sabalenka is a Gucci face, Fritz is a Boss ambassador, and Novak Djokovic reps Lacoste.
points: With Naomi Osaka, Coco Gauff, and Venus Williams in play, don’t expect traditional tennis whites on the hard court.

articles.title: Amal Clooney Isn’t Letting Go of Boho Just Yet
articles.summary: The Clooneys departed Venice Film Festival—but not without turning one last look. Of course, Amal Clooney opted for a summer staple.
body: Amal Clooney is truly at her best at Venice Film Festival: glamorous vintage gowns, sparkly party-ready minis, layers of Cartier jewels, and blown out Old Hollywood curls to boot. For 2026, she embraced sequins, spots, and some serious stilettos.
A close second? Her Euro summer style, which leans more boho, floaty looks perfect for seeing out the hot months at Lake Como.

The Clooneys were photographed today (September 5) departing the Italian city dressed much more casually—well…as casual as Amal Clooney is ever going to get. She wore a simple black tank top paired with an Elie Saab snake-print silk maxi skirt that featured a high leg slit, cinched at the waist with a low-slung brown belt. She added chunky platform sandals and Cartier bracelets, and toted a tan Chloé Bracelet bag. Her hair, as per, was swept into a deep side part, and she sported her signature oversized sunglasses.
Hand in clasped hand, George strode beside her in a navy blue polo, cream trousers, his favorite beige moccasins, and black aviators.
